name: AOZ1282CI
title: 1.2 A non-synchronous buck regulator, 4.5 V to 36 V input, 450 kHz, SOT23-6L
summary: The AOZ1282CI is a step-down converter in a six-lead SOT23 that switches an on-chip 420 mΩ N-channel high-side MOSFET at a fixed 450 kHz under current-mode control, with an external Schottky diode as the low-side rectifier and a bootstrap capacitor driving the gate. It runs from 4.5 V to 36 V, delivers up to 1.2 A continuous, and regulates FB to 0.8 V so the output can be set from 0.8 V to 0.85 × VIN with two resistors. Compensation and soft start are built in; protection covers cycle-by-cycle current limit, hiccup short-circuit shutdown, UVLO and thermal shutdown.

circuits.title: 1.2A Buck Regulator
circuits.description: A step-down converter from VIN to an adjustable VOUT. C1 bypasses the input at VIN and GND. The chip's switch pulls LX up to VIN; L1 carries the current on to the output capacitor C2, and D1 takes the inductor current from ground while the switch is off. C3, between BST and LX, supplies the high-side gate drive. R1 and R2 divide VOUT down to the 0.8 V that FB regulates. EN switches the converter on and off.

operation.text: Current-mode control at a fixed frequency set by an internal oscillator, 450 kHz, in continuous conduction at steady state. The switch current is sensed from the voltage across the high-side NMOS. A transconductance error amplifier compares FB with the 0.8 V reference; its output is compared with the sensed current plus a compensation ramp. The switch turns on each cycle and turns off once the current signal crosses the error voltage, after which the inductor current flows through the external Schottky diode. Compensation is internal.

Soft start begins once VIN is above the UVLO threshold and EN is high; the output then ramps to regulation in about 400 µs, a time fixed inside the part. EN is active high: above 1.2 V the part runs, below 0.4 V it is off. Tie EN to VIN when the enable function is not needed; grounding it disables the converter. EN must not be left open.
The converter starts when VIN rises past 2.9 V and stops switching when VIN falls below 2.3 V.

The sensed switch current also sets a cycle-by-cycle limit of 1.9 A nominal. When it is reached the switch turns off at once for the rest of that cycle, capping the peak and so the average inductor current; the output voltage falls as the duty cycle shrinks.
When FB falls below 0.2 V the converter shuts down and retries in hiccup mode, which keeps the average inductor current low. Once the short is removed it starts again through soft start.
Above a junction temperature of 150 °C the control circuit and the high-side NMOS shut down; the part restarts through soft start when the junction cools to 110 °C.

Place it across VIN and GND. Its voltage rating must exceed the highest input voltage plus ripple, and its ripple current rating must exceed ICIN_RMS at the worst operating point, which is 0.5 × IOUT at VOUT = VIN / 2. Ceramic is preferred, its ESR being low and its ripple current capacity high; X5R or X7R for their temperature and voltage behaviour; low-ESR tantalum or aluminium electrolytic may also be used. Capacitor ripple current ratings rest on a lifetime figure and may need further derating.

Inductance, frequency and the input and output voltages set the ripple current. A larger inductance lowers ripple, core loss and RMS current in the inductor and switches, at the cost of a bigger part. The inductor must carry the peak current without saturating at the highest operating temperature, and its conduction loss must suit the thermal and efficiency budget. Shielded parts radiate less EMI and cost more than unshielded ones. Coilcraft, Elytone and Murata offer suitable surface-mount inductors.

Choose it by DC voltage rating, output ripple and ripple current. Its voltage rating must exceed the highest output voltage including ripple, with derating for long life. Ripple current in it is usually small, but a very small inductor with high ripple current can overstress it. X5R or X7R ceramic keeps ripple low over temperature; low-ESR tantalum or aluminium electrolytic may also be used.

The external diode carries the inductor current while the switch is off. A Schottky part is recommended for its low forward drop and recovery loss. Its reverse voltage rating must exceed the highest input voltage and its current rating the highest load current.

Two loops carry pulsed current: input capacitor, VIN, LX, inductor, output capacitor and load, back through ground, while the switch is on; and inductor, output capacitor and load, diode anode to cathode, while the diode conducts. Keep both loop areas small to cut noise and raise efficiency. A ground plane is strongly recommended, tying together the GND pin and both the input and output capacitors. Put the input capacitor right at VIN and GND, the inductor right at LX and the output capacitor, and keep the diode connection between LX and GND short and wide. Keep the feedback resistors and any compensation parts close to the chip and sensitive traces away from LX. Give VIN, LX and above all GND as much copper as possible for heat, and flood spare board area with copper tied to a steady DC node such as VIN, GND or VOUT.

The AOZ1282CI, the Schottky diode and the inductor dissipate most of the power. The part's own dissipation and θJA give the junction temperature, which may not exceed 150 °C and so limits load current. The PCB layout has a strong effect on the thermal performance.
